title: feat(types): the app document refuses `mobileNavMode` by name (objectui#11363)
body:
Part of #11363
Clause-②: no

Step B+ of objectui#11363 (seat answer `5937316485`, claim amendment `5938266908`): objectui's app document refuses `mobileNavMode` by name, which is the answer `@objectstack/spec`'s strict `AppSchema` already gives. Step B, the guide correction, is draft PR objectui#11397, which is waiting on an authorized approval. The seat ends the card itself once both have merged, so this PR says `Part of`.

## What changes

- `packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts`: `AppComponentSchema` declares `mobileNavMode` as a named refusal (`z.never`, `invalid_type` at the key's own path), next to `logo` and `favicon`. The message opens with the spec's own sentence, "Unrecognized key(s) on this app: `mobileNavMode`.", and names the two places the mode is read: the `mobileNavMode` prop of `AppSchemaRenderer` and the `mobileNavMode` key of an `app-schema-renderer` node.
- `packages/types/src/app.ts`: the TS twin `mobileNavMode?: never`, matching the `logo?: never` twin.
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/page-app-dashboard-spec-parity.test.ts`: the App row's `local` ledger lists `mobileNavMode` with the app's other local refusals.
- A new pin, `packages/types/src/__tests__/app-mobile-nav-mode-refusal-11363.test.ts`, and `.changeset/11363-app-face-refuses-mobile-nav-mode.md` (`@object-ui/types`: minor). The breaking semantics are in its body, per AGENTS.md §9's no-major rule; the `logo` changeset is the nearest example.

Not touched: `AppSchemaRenderer`, the `app-schema-renderer` registration, and the guide (`skills/**`, PR objectui#11397).

## One departure from the ruling's wording: `retirementTombstone`, not `aliasKeyRefusal`

The amendment names "the `aliasKeyRefusal` construct `logo` / `favicon` already use". That helper always composes "Did you mean `ALIAS` → `CANONICAL`?", and its `canonical` parameter is documented as "the declared member the author meant". No member of the app document means a mobile navigation mode. The remedy is a different channel (a component prop, or another node type), not a sibling spelling. The spec doesn't say that sentence for this key either. Measured on `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0, it answers `logo` with "Unrecognized key(s) on this app: `logo`. Did you mean `logo` → `branding`? …" and `mobileNavMode` with only "Unrecognized key(s) on this app: `mobileNavMode`. Until this shape was closed, …". The tree already records the same reasoning for `MenuItemSchema.shortcut`; its pin says the helper "could only be made to say something untrue" there.

So the arm uses `retirementTombstone`, the sibling helper built on the same `z.never` primitive. The issue code and path, the `?: never` twin and the accept set are all the same. Its guidance opens with the spec's lead sentence verbatim. That is what `aliasKeyRefusal` exists to do ("so an author meets the same remedy on both faces"), minus the alias sentence the platform does not say. The pin reads that sentence from the spec at run time and asserts that the mirror's message starts with it. If the seat wants the literal helper anyway, it would need a canonical argument to name, and none exists. Switching would be a one-line change.

## Zone 2 measurements (each premise checked first)

1. **The base reproduces.** At `d59f11c0`, `AppComponentSchema.safeParse` of an app document with `mobileNavMode` set to `'bottom_nav'`, `'drawer'` or a typo succeeds and keeps the key in `.data`. So does the control `totallyMadeUpKey`. `'mobileNavMode' in AppComponentSchema.shape` is `false` (control: `layout` is `true`). Spec 17.5.0's `AppSchema` answers `unrecognized_keys` with keys `['mobileNavMode']` for every value. The control `notAKey` is refused the same way, and the minimal app passes.
2. **`AppComponentSchema` does not judge the node channel.** The same probe ran through all five judges (`AppComponentSchema`, `AnyComponentSchema`, `SchemaNodeSchema`, `StrictAnyComponentSchema`, `StrictSchemaNodeSchema`), before and after the change. Every `app-schema-renderer` row is byte-identical, with or without `mobileNavMode`, because no arm of the component union claims that type literal. Only the app-document rows move.
   - At runtime, on the changed tree, a one-shot probe (real `SchemaRenderer` plus `registerLayout()`, deleted after the run) drew the bottom bar for an `app-schema-renderer` node carrying `mobileNavMode: 'bottom_nav'`, with the sidebar and title rendered. It drew no bar for the same node without the key. In the same run, the app document was refused at `mobileNavMode`.
   - A new pin block asserts that the key adds no issue to such a node, on the validator face and on the strict face. An arm for that node type derived from this schema would turn it red.
3. **There are no producers.** In objectui at `d59f11c0`, `mobileNavMode` appears 0 times in `examples/`, `content/` and `apps/`. The control: the app documents in `content/docs` do match `navigation`. The remaining hits are the prop, the registration, their tests, and the guide sentence that objectui#11397 rewrites. In objectstack `origin/main` `862f12c`, outside CHANGELOGs, there are 0 hits (control: `mobileNavigation` matches 3 or more files).
4. **Reach of the shadowed `schema` input:** see Acceptance notes.

Public door: `objectui validate` (run from source, so `safeValidateSchema` on the built tree) now exits 1 on an app document carrying `mobileNavMode`. It prints the message above with `Path: mobileNavMode` and `Code: invalid_type`, and the control document exits 0. Before this change the same validator kept the key (measurement 1).

An intended side effect on the strict authoring face: it already refused the key, but only as a bare `unrecognized_keys` at the root ("Unrecognized key: …"). Now it refuses the key by name, at the key's path, with the message above.

## Verification (head `c17e6220`)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build`: exit 0 (dist completeness: 140 files).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check`, all three programs including `tsconfig.test.json`: exit 0.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/`: 318 files, 8410 tests passed.
- The other suites that import `AppComponentSchema` or the app face, or judge app documents (layout, runner, components, cli validate and scripts; 23 files): 289 tests passed.
- `eslint .` in `packages/types`: 395 files, 0 errors. The one warning on `app.zod.ts` is a pre-existing `no-explicit-any` above this change.
- These gates exit 0: `check:spec-symbols`, `check:doc-types`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:control-bytes`, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `changeset:check`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:component-surface-parity`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals` and `check:installed-pin-claims`. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the five paths answers NOT GOVERNED.
- NOT MEASURED, because each needs sibling packages built first:
  - `check:spec-floors`: its 20 findings are all `no-artifact` on unbuilt siblings. It inspected the 140 files of `@object-ui/types` and found nothing.
  - `check:readme-exports`.
  - `check:doc-snippets` and `check:doc-examples`: this diff can only move a doc snippet that writes `mobileNavMode`, and `content/` has none.

  CI runs all four.

**Ablations**, from the committed state, through `ablation-replace.mjs` (it proves the mutation landed and that the restore matches HEAD's blob):
- Delete the zod arm: the new pin goes 10 failed, 34 passed. The mirror rows (3 values plus the message row) and the `safeValidateSchema` and strict-face rows (3 each) fail. The node, control and spec rows stay green. Restored: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- Delete the TS twin: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` fails with TS2578 (unused `@ts-expect-error`) in the new pin. The type-level ledger in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` also fails, because the mirror declares the key and the twin does not. Restored the same way.

## Acceptance notes

- **The `app-schema-renderer` registration's `schema` input (carried from review `5938161085`): a reach reading only; not fixed here.** The registration declares `{ name: 'schema', type: 'object' }`. Read live, its inputs are `schema` (object), `basePath` (string) and `mobileNavMode` (enum), and it sets no `tier`. `SchemaRenderer` strips an authored `schema` off the node and passes the node itself as the component's `schema`. Measured in the one-shot probe:
  - The published manifest does not carry the node. `ComponentRegistry.getPublicConfigs()`, which `gen-manifest.ts` serialises into `sdui.manifest.json`, has 80 entries and `app-schema-renderer` is not among them (control: `text` is).
  - The JSX-page compiler does steer authors into the nested form. The probe built the manifest from the live registry the way `renderers/layout/page.tsx` builds it:
    - a nested `schema={{ title: "Acme CRM" }}` gets 0 diagnostics;
    - the working top-level form, `title="Acme CRM"`, gets an `unknown-prop` warning;
    - control: `schema="Acme CRM"` gets `type-mismatch`, so the input is judged.

    Rendered, the nested form draws an empty shell (no title, no navigation), and the top-level form draws both.
  - `content/docs/guide/layout.md` says the node "builds branding and sidebar navigation from an `AppSchema` JSON document", next to "declaring its `inputs`". It has no JSON example, so it suggests the nested form without teaching it.
  - No stored `app-schema-renderer` node or page is known to exist.
  - Possible family: `dashboard-editor` (`@object-ui/plugin-designer`) also declares a `schema` input, which the same `SchemaRenderer` destructure would shadow. That is a source reading only; it was not measured.
- No docs page names `mobileNavMode`, so no docs edit is owed. The guide is step B.
